title: receiptSharing vs receiveTypingIndicators naming direction asymmetry
description: The Chat object has two opt-out preference fields that name opposite directions for similar controls. 'receiveTypingIndicators' uses receive-side framing (the owner controls what they receive). 'receiptSharing' uses send-side framing (the owner controls what they share). A reader scanning Chat fields must context-switch between two conceptual frames for structurally parallel opt-out preferences. Concretely: 'receiveTypingIndicators: false' means 'do not receive typing events from others'; 'receiptSharing: false' means 'do not send read receipts to others'. Suggested improvement: pick one framing and apply it consistently. The receive-side pattern ('receiveReadReceipts' or 'receiveReceipts') matches the existing 'receiveTypingIndicators'. Alternatively, adopt send-side framing for both ('shareTypingIndicators', 'shareReceipts'). The current mix is not itself wrong but reduces readability for implementors scanning the Chat field list. Location: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00.md Chat object fields ~lines 438-442 (receiveTypingIndicators and receiptSharing) and PresenceStatus ~line 784 (receiptSharing).
close_reason: Opinion: both names are unambiguous, naming asymmetry is stylistic only
